messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on Dedicated cluster 'eu-west-2-dedicated-3' for tenant AureliaBank — error-rate 5m avg = 12.4% (baseline 0.3%). Auto-escalation to P1.
anya_oncall: I’m on it — paging eng-sre and eng-runtime. grabbing logs now.
samir_platform: oncall here. initial thought: gateway timeouts + model-evictions? seeing a spike in KV eviction metrics too.
miguel_runtime: pinged. joining. do we have tenant id and which model/container?
anya_oncall: tenant=aurelia-bank-prod id=tb_7782. Endpoint shard eu-west-2-dedicated-3. Model pinned: gptx-7b-q8.
lia_csm: lia_csm here — customer reported latency from their app, they’re seeing errors in production. I’ve told them we’re investigating and will update in 15.
anya_oncall: quick dumps: 
```
kubectl -n redwood logs svc/dedicated-gateway-eu-west-2-3 --since=2m | grep tb_7782 | tail -n 20
[2026-03-15T16:12:02Z] 500 gateway timeout tb_7782 call_id=ck_1a2b
[2026-03-15T16:12:03Z] 502 upstream reset tb_7782 shard=eu-west-2-3
[2026-03-15T16:12:05Z] 504 model inference timeout tb_7782 seq=64
```
anya_oncall: also seeing KV cache thrash with high miss rate ~87% for that tenant, and GPU busy %.

miguel_runtime: that KV miss + model timeouts smells like a hot-tenant causing batch queue growth and frequent KV evictions. check host-level GPU load and batching queue depth.
alex_infra: checking node metrics: one pool node has GPU utilization 98% and mem pressure, OOMs on the model runtime not yet but high swap.
samir_platform: can we confirm noisy-tenant vs downstream network flakiness? Are other tenants affected?
anya_oncall: other tenants on the same shard: 8 tenants, error rates stable for others. traffic for AureliaBank jumped x8 in last 10m per request-rate graph.
miguel_runtime: ok noisy-tenant. mitigation options: 1) apply tenant-level QOS (shed / throttle) 2) move their traffic to a spare shard 3) scale up capacity / preempt low-priority workloads 4) fallback their traffic to a smaller model (gptx-3b) temporarily.
samir_platform: do we have spare capacity in the region? alex_infra?
alex_infra: we have one warm reserve node but adding it to dedicated pool requires ~3 min to attach and warm model weights. can do immediate traffic reroute to dedicated-fallback cluster in another AZ which has gptx-7b warm. cross-az adds ~20ms latency but better than 5xx.
anya_oncall: priority: reduce customer impact quickly. I propose immediate tenant throttling to ~20% of current qps + spawn cross-az reroute for failover. then assess longer-term move/scale.
miguel_runtime: agree. I’ll open a canary route to eu-west-2-dedicated-1 for tb_7782 with weight 10% then 50%. routing command: 
```
# route api
redwood route create --tenant tb_7782 --to-shard eu-west-2-dedicated-1 --weight 10 --note "incident 3415009999"
```
anya_oncall: executing tenant throttle now: 
```
redwood qos set --tenant tb_7782 --max-qps 180 --reason "emergency throttle: high 5xx"
```
deploy-bot: QoS update accepted. previous max-qps=920 -> new max-qps=180.
samir_platform: miguel, once you have canary routing in place we can increase weight and monitor 5xx. lia, can you tell AureliaBank we’re throttling to protect stability and routing some traffic to fallback? set expectation 10–20% increased latency, reduced error rate within 10–15m.
lia_csm: calling them now. putting short message in support channel and pinging their eng. will request immediate throttling acknowledgement.
miguel_runtime: canary route created: tracking logs now. initial 10% traffic shows 5xx -> 1.2%, latency +18ms. increasing to 50%.
anya_oncall: increasing route to 50%... done. observing aggregated 5xx drop to 3.6% (still above baseline). KV miss for tb_7782 on original shard down from 87% -> 62% (less pressure).
samir_platform: good. next step: preempt any low-priority batch jobs on original shard to free GPU. alex, can you evict batch workloads?
alex_infra: called eviction API: 
```
infra preempt --shard eu-west-2-dedicated-3 --policy low-priority-batch --dry-run=false
```
preemption triggered, batch pods terminating. expected free GPU in ~45s.
anya_oncall: preempted. GPUs showing drop to 70% util now. queue depth down. 5xx trending down to 1.0% across the shard.
miguel_runtime: pulling a quick remediation checklist for follow-up: 
- keep canary route at 50% until error stable <0.5% for 10m
- keep QoS limit until normal traffic pattern verified
- run tenant traffic analysis for why abrupt spike (rate-limiter bypass? job misconfig?)
- schedule capacity increase or tenant isolation if this repeats
- post-incident follow-up with AureliaBank + SRE & runtime owners

anya_oncall: lia, any customer impact notes? SLA breach?
lia_csm: AureliaBank reported 12% request failures and some aborted payment requests. their SLO is 99.9% per endpoint — this is a partial SLO breach for the 15m window. they’ve escalated to their ops lead and want timeline. I told them 2 hours for full recovery plan and we’d share RCA within 72h.
samir_platform: recording incident P1. tagging runtime & infra for RCA. miguel, alex — please own remediation items. I’ll own postmortem and timeline.
miguel_runtime: will take model & routing remediation. starting collection of traces and KV metrics.
alex_infra: I’ll document preemption steps and warm-capacity timeline.
anya_oncall: handing off to night oncall (samir) — I’m staying as backup for 30m. if 5xx >1% alert again.
samir_platform: acknowledged. I’ll keep watch and coordinate follow-ups. nice work team. :thumbsup:
lia_csm: I’ve updated the customer and logged incident reference 3415009999. will coordinate a customer postmortem call for tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident 3415009999 status update: mitigated -> error-rate stabilized at 0.4% across shard. P1 remains open for RCA. Next update scheduled in 30m. :white_check_mark:
